newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin confirms Kvashnin as military's number two.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin confirms Kvashnin as military's number two.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday confirmed General Anatoly Kvashnin as chief of the general staff, number two in Russia's armed forces after the defence minister.
Kvashnin stepped in as acting chief of general staff in late May, after Yeltsin suddenly sacked his predecessor Viktor Samsonov along with then-defence minister Igor Rodionov.
The Kremlin said Yeltsin had appointed Kvashnin by decree on Thursday to the position, which makes him deputy to new defence minister Igor Sergeyev.

Yeltsin accused their predecessors of dragging their feet over urgently-needed military reforms and urged them to crack down on high-level corruption and channel resouces into modernising and cutting back the armed forces.
Yet when Kvashnin first took on the general staff role last month, analysts said he was part of the old school.
Kvashnin, 50, is former head of the North Caucasus military district which covers Chechnya, where Moscow conducted a disastrous military campaign for 21 months until last August.
"Kvashnin belongs to the group of "elite generals" faithful to Soviet military doctrine," the Sevodnya liberal daily said.

"His current appointment is most likely linked to Yeltsin's wish to provide some counterbalance to the rapidly strengthening "technocrats team" and also to the fact that the president knows Kvashnin well," it said. "All this suggests that the personnel struggle in the General Staff is far from over."
